records.title: Modulation and Power Losses of a Stacked Polyphase Bridge Converter
records.topology: Stacked polyphase bridge: N series-connected two-level, three-phase submodules
records.winding_configuration: 12 windings; four independent three-phase winding sets
records.balancing_requirement: Submodule capacitor-voltage balancing using outer voltage control
records.fault_tolerance: One faulty submodule can be bypassed
records.post_fault_capability: Three remaining submodules continue supplying output power after transient
records.test_conditions: 200 V DC supply; 50 V per submodule; 6 A AC peak current; 20 kHz switching; 50 Hz fundamental; four-submodule motor test
main_advantages: Modular voltage scaling with low-voltage semiconductors
Demonstrated bypass operation after one submodule fault
Carrier phase shifting reduces DC-side current harmonics and capacitance requirements
main_limitations: Inspected PDF is not the expected modulation-and-power-losses paper
Efficiency, losses, rated power, power density, and device ratings not reported
missing_information: Rated and peak power not reported
Semiconductor voltage and current ratings not reported

records.title: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase Three-Level Flying Capacitor and Stacked Polyphase Bridge GaN Inverter Systems for Integrated Motor Drives
records.topology: Three-level flying-capacitor converter versus two series-stacked two-level three-phase converters
records.modulation_method: Phase-shifted PWM for 3L-FCC; field-oriented control with active midpoint balancing for 2L-SSC
records.balancing_requirement: Flying-capacitor natural balancing may require active balancing; split DC-link midpoint active balancing for 2L-SSC
records.common_mode_information: Ideal 2L-SSC common-mode cancellation; 100 ns mismatch produces ±66.7 V spikes
records.test_conditions: 800 V DC link; 7.5 kW nominal output; 15 A nominal peak phase current; 45 A peak for 3 s overload; 35 kHz device switching; calculated CM-choke efficiency comparison
main_advantages: 2L-SSC common-mode choke approximately 30% of 3L-FCC volume and nominal losses
Lower semiconductor blocking requirement per stacked inverter
main_limitations: Efficiency and volume results largely calculated or simulated
2L-SSC requires dual-winding motor and potentially doubled output-filter volume/losses
Common-mode cancellation is sensitive to timing mismatch and motor asymmetry
End-to-end experimental drive validation not reported
missing_information: Complete hardware drive demonstration not reported
Fault tolerance and post-fault capability not reported
Cooling details insufficient for a complete system comparison

records.title: Dynamic multi-agent dc-bus reconfiguration in modular motor drives with a stacked polyphase bridge converter
records.topology: Multiple series-connected three-phase two-level voltage-source inverters
records.winding_configuration: Five three-phase agents; 15 pole drive units
records.modulation_method: Three-phase vector PI current control with decentralized dynamic-average-consensus balancing
records.balancing_requirement: Decentralized capacitor-voltage balancing using local measurements and neighbour communication
records.post_fault_capability: Four active agents continue operation; torque reduced by factor 4/5 without interruption
records.test_conditions: 700 rpm; 7 A q-axis current reference; 240 V DC bus; 10 kHz switching/sampling; 2 kHz balancing update; 220 μF per-agent capacitors
main_advantages: Demonstrated dynamic agent isolation and reactivation
Maintains torque without interruption after agent isolation
main_limitations: Final DC-link short-circuit step not experimentally validated
Torque demand is reduced after isolation
Decentralization implemented on one FPGA rather than physically distributed controllers
Efficiency, losses, power density, device ratings, and cooling not reported
missing_information: Semiconductor voltage and current ratings not reported

records.title: Comparison of optimized motor-inverter systems using a Stacked Polyphase Bridge Converter combined with a 3-, 6-, 9-, or 12-phase PMSM
records.winding_configuration: Compared 3-, 6-, 9-, and 12-phase systems; non-phase-aligned winding displacements of 30°, 40°, and 15°
records.cooling_method: Heat sink included in modeled system volume; thermal assumptions specified
records.test_conditions: 50 Nm rated torque; 300 rpm rated speed; 55 °C ambient; 125 °C maximum junction temperature; modeled switching-frequency range 1–100 kHz
main_advantages: Modeled average 0.70% increase in maximum efficiency for multiphase configurations
Modeled average 3.8% increase in maximum power density
Modular SPB architecture supports multiple phase counts
main_limitations: No experimental hardware validation
Absolute efficiency and power-density values not extracted
Multiphase combined motor-converter modularity reported as practically infeasible
Switching-frequency tradeoff between motor and converter losses
missing_information: Rated and peak power not reported
Representative DC-link voltage depends on configuration and is not unique
Switching frequency optimum not reported as one value
Power density absolute value not reported
Fault tolerance and post-fault capability not reported

records.title: Multi-Agent Control Scheme for Power Distribution in a Multi-Three-Phase Motor Drive Fed by a Stacked Polyphase Bridges Converter
records.winding_configuration: 15 stator coils divided into five three-phase winding sets with separate neutral points
records.modulation_method: Decentralized PI current control with static/dynamic average consensus and active voltage balancers
records.test_conditions: 240 V total DC bus; approximately 48 V per agent in parallel validation; communication frequencies 2 kHz and 1 kHz; measurements recorded at 10 kHz
main_advantages: Supports unequal and time-varying torque sharing
main_limitations: All controllers implemented on a single FPGA
Torque ripple near approximately 450 rpm due to drive resonances
Efficiency, power density, cooling, EMI, and post-fault results not reported
Demonstrated loss-aware cost model was not experimentally validated for converter-loss reduction
missing_information: Semiconductor voltage and current ratings not verified
Fault tolerance and post-fault capability not reported

records.title: Design and Experimental Validation of a High-Power-Density GaN-Based Inverter Module for Integrated Modular Motor Drives in All-Electric Aircraft Applications
records.topology: 18 modular full-bridge converters arranged as six three-phase subsets
records.machine_type: Three-phase PMSM target system; motor coil substituted by inductors during test
records.winding_configuration: 18 modules dedicated to 18 stator coil pairs; six three-phase subsets
records.cooling_method: Experimental off-the-shelf fan-cooled heat sink, 0.15 °C/W; target heat-pipe cooling not fully explored
records.common_mode_information: PCB busbar and measured switching overshoot; quantitative EMI performance not reported
records.test_conditions: 166.67 V DC link; 20 kHz switching; 1250 Hz fundamental; 268 A rms load; 16 min continuous test; 189.25 W module loss; 77.51 °C average near FETs and 104.3 °C maximum PCB temperature
main_advantages: Achieved 43.96 kW/kg gravimetric power density excluding thermal-management system
Demonstrated low overshoot with 0.7 nH total loop inductance
main_limitations: No experimental motor operation; inductors substituted for motor coils
Individual device current rating not reliably available
Quantitative EMI and fault-tolerance results not reported
Target heat-pipe cooling not experimentally validated
Reported power density is gravimetric, not volumetric
missing_information: Total system DC-link voltage not clearly reported
Fault tolerance and post-fault capability not reported
